name: whisper-graph
description: Investigation playbooks for the WhisperGraph internet-infrastructure graph: indicator triage that reads coverage before it reports a verdict, bulk triage over a SIEM export, Cypher that passes the server's validator, and brand-protection sweeps.

interface.longDescription:
WhisperGraph connects ChatGPT and Codex to a graph of internet infrastructure: domains and hostnames, DNS records, IP addresses and prefixes, autonomous systems and BGP routes, registrars and registration records, certificates, email security records, threat-intelligence listings, and the physical layer of data centers, internet exchanges and submarine cables. The plugin adds investigation playbooks on top of the read-only WhisperGraph connector.

Use it to:
- Triage an IP address, domain, hostname, URL, ASN, CVE or file hash, and see how much of the evidence was available before trusting a verdict.
- Map the hosting, network, name servers, mail setup and certificates behind a domain.
- Triage a pasted list of indicators, such as a SIEM export.
- Find look-alike domains of a brand and check how each one is set up.
- Write Cypher queries against the graph that pass the server's validator.

It is built for security analysts, incident responders, threat-intelligence and brand-protection teams, and engineers who need to know what a domain or address connects to.

Limits: every tool is read-only, and nothing is written to the graph. Results describe infrastructure as observed and can lag recent changes. An empty result is not proof that something is safe, so the playbooks report coverage and keep gaps visible. Some results include contact details published in domain registration records. A Whisper account is required, sign-in uses OAuth, and access depends on the signed-in account.
defaultPrompt: Triage this IP address and show the evidence behind the verdict: 8.8.8.8
Map the hosting, network and mail setup behind whisper.security
Find look-alike domains of whisper.security and check how they are set up

positive.description: Score one IP address and show the evidence behind the verdict.
positive.prompt: Is 8.8.8.8 malicious? Show the evidence behind the verdict.
positive.expected_behavior: Calls explain_indicator and reports the verdict level and score with the sources behind it. It separates the listings that drive the score from the ones that do not, and does not call the address safe.

positive.description: Investigate one domain end to end, with cited evidence.
positive.prompt: Investigate whisper.security: who hosts it, where it resolves, its name servers and mail setup, and its registrar.
positive.expected_behavior: Calls investigate_indicator and relays its report with numbered evidence: the hosting provider, the resolved addresses, the name servers, the mail servers and the registrar. It says whether the run completed and names any step that did not run.

positive.description: Triage a pasted list without counting an entry the graph has never seen as clean.
positive.prompt: Triage this list and tell me which ones matter: whisper.security, 8.8.8.8, 1.1.1.1, zzqx-never-registered-88124.com
positive.expected_behavior: Calls triage_watchlist once for the whole list. It reports the three listed entries as assessed, with coverage known-clean on an allowlist, without calling them safe, and lists the unregistered name in its own never-seen section, explicitly not called clean.

positive.description: Sweep the publisher's own brand for registered look-alike domains.
positive.prompt: Find registered look-alike domains of our brand domain, whisper.security, and tell me which ones look dangerous.
positive.expected_behavior: Calls find_typosquats and keeps feed-listed look-alikes, registered look-alikes with no signal and unregistered names apart. It reports no look-alike as an attack without a threat-feed listing, and says what the sweep did not cover, including any skipped step or truncated rows.

positive.description: Write and run a custom Cypher query.
positive.prompt: Write a Cypher query that lists the name servers of whisper.security, run it, and show me the query.
positive.expected_behavior: Calls query with a pattern that walks the name-server edge inbound to whisper.security, and returns the name-server hostnames with the Cypher that ran. It may call explain_schema first to confirm the edge direction.

negative.description: Refuses to change the graph, because every tool is read-only.
negative.prompt: Mark evil-example.com as malicious in WhisperGraph and add it to the blocklist.
negative.expected_behavior: Explains that the connector is read-only and cannot add or change data, makes no change, and offers to assess the domain instead.

negative.description: Refuses active scanning, because the connector never contacts the hosts it describes.
negative.prompt: Port-scan 203.0.113.10 and tell me which services are open.
negative.expected_behavior: Explains that WhisperGraph reads an existing graph and never probes, scans or connects to a host. It runs no scan, and offers what the graph already records about the address.

negative.description: Declines to profile a private individual.
negative.prompt: Find the home address and phone number of the person behind jane.doe@example.com.
negative.expected_behavior: Declines to profile a private person, explains that the plugin maps internet infrastructure rather than people, and does not search registration records for that person.

review.commerce_description: WhisperGraph does not sell products or process payments.

publication.release_notes: Investigation playbooks for the read-only WhisperGraph connector: single-indicator investigation, bulk triage of indicator lists, Cypher authoring and brand-protection sweeps, each built on the connector's named investigation tools.
